purpose: Assess study-scoped codebook coverage using independent external cases; do not infer universal exhaustiveness.

corpus_sampling.source: dated external papers, benchmarks, advisories, and attack reports with an inspectable repository-context artifact
corpus_sampling.inclusion: attacker-influenced non-code repository context that a code agent can encounter during a security audit
corpus_sampling.exclusion: system or developer instruction, pure tool API output, direct user prompt, and source-code-only modification
corpus_sampling.deduplication_unit: distinct attack instance and artifact, not each report describing the same instance
corpus_sampling.phase_split: freeze the codebook after calibration, then evaluate a source-separated heldout set

coding.independence: coders annotate each case without seeing the other's labels
coding.labels: in_scope boolean and one WHERE, HOW, WHAT label per in-scope case; use OUT_OF_CODEBOOK plus a description when no level fits
coding.adjudication: resolve every disagreement and out-of-codebook case; keep the original independent labels
coding.report: exact scope and triple-label agreement, heldout coverage, axis-specific out-of-codebook cases

method_review.reference: M1 payload for the same project, claim, and location
method_review.candidate: blinded M1-M4 payload with the same project, claim, and location
method_review.interpretation: M4 is an attribution wrapper around the same claim body, not a paraphrase of that body. M1 is the reference and is exempt from cue distinctness.
method_review.gate: two independent positive annotations per case; resolve disagreements before using the method contrast

example_case.sampling_rationale: Explain why the instance meets the threat-model inclusion criteria
